title.value: An act to add Chapter 12.5 (commencing with Section 108945) to Part 3 of Division 104 of the Health and Safety Code, relating to product safety. Juvenile Products
title.provenance: An act to add Chapter 12.5 (commencing with Section 108945) to Part 3 of Division 104 of the Health and Safety Code, relating to product safety. Juvenile Products

location.provenance: The people of the State of California do enact as follows:

status.provenance: Approved by Governor October 5, 2021. Filed with Secretary of State October 5, 2021.

date.provenance: Approved by Governor October 5, 2021. Filed with Secretary of State October 5, 2021.

pfas_definition.provenance: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) means a class of fluorinated organic chemicals containing at least one fully fluorinated carbon atom.

type.provenance: On and after July 1, 2023, a person, including, but not limited to, a manufacturer, shall not sell or distribute in commerce in this state any new, not previously owned, juvenile product that contains regulated PFAS chemicals.

who.provenance: A person, including, but not limited to, a manufacturer

action.provenance: shall not sell or distribute in commerce

products.provenance: any new, not previously owned, juvenile product

currently_unavoidable.provenance: The bill specifies concentrations (up to 100 parts per million) at which PFAS are regulated, implying that uses below this level are not considered currently unavoidable.

intentionally_added.provenance: Regulated PFAS includes those that a manufacturer has intentionally added to a product.

type.provenance: A manufacturer shall use the least toxic alternative when replacing PFAS chemicals in a juvenile product.

action.provenance: use the least toxic alternative when replacing PFAS chemicals

currently_unavoidable.provenance: This regulation pertains to the replacement of PFAS, implying that their use is not currently unavoidable.

intentionally_added.provenance: The regulation pertains to replacing intentionally added PFAS.
